## Summary

**MOVZ2** (Move two with Zero fill): Move a pair & Zero extend.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `Memory → destination pair` |
| Syntax | `MOVZ2.B <ea>,b:c`<br>`MOVZ2.W <ea>,b:c` |
| Short | Move a pair & Zero extend. |
| Description | Move from memory to two registers and zero fill to long. Size byte or word. |
| Condition codes | are taken from b, the first. |

### Condition codes

| X | N | Z | V | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| – | * | * | 0 | 0 |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–8 | `00001110` |
| 1 | 7–6 | Size |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | B |
| 2 | 11–10 | `00` |
| 2 | 9–6 | C |
| 2 | 5–0 | `010010` |

- S=Size 0=byte, 1=word.
- B & C: data or address-register.

### Example

```asm
    movz2.w    (a0),d2:d3
```

- ea (a0) memory content where a0 points to

```text
01 23 45 67 89 AB CD EF
Result:
b d2 & d3: .. .. .. .. 00 00 01 23
           .. .. .. .. 00 00 45 67
```

### Notes

- movem extends signed. move2 does not extend.
- &lt;ea&gt; must refer to memory, else unexpected result.
- movz2 is not in V2

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no MOVZ2. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DO use a memory `<ea>`: other modes give unexpected results.
- DON'T use MOVZ2 on V2 cores: it is not in V2.
